$comment: Generated by website-builder from a live crawl. Categories and section names are heuristics (see meta.generatedBy); edit this file, then re-run `node validate.mjs && node build.mjs`.

meta.generatedBy: website-builder: section names come from the page's own markup (data attributes, React component names, ids, classes, landmarks); categories are keyword heuristics; reconciled with design-repo 0.2.0 (sections, categories, templates and full route lists are taken from design-repo/)

categories.CONTENT: The substantive body of a page: articles, listings, resources and general sections.
categories.HERO: Page-opening block: the main headline (h1) and first call to action.
categories.SUPPORT: Questions and contact: FAQs, help, forms.
categories.SHELL: Site chrome: navigation, header, footer, announcement bars and other elements carried across pages.
categories.FEATURES: Product explanation: capabilities, benefits, workflows and integrations.
categories.PROOF: Trust evidence: customer logos, quotes, ratings.
categories.COMMERCE: Pricing and plans so the visitor can choose.

commerce.pricing-plans.description: Lets a visitor compare the three monthly plans (Pro, Ultra, Max) by description, price and included credits, and start the download from any of them. Plan name is items[].title, its description is items[].body; price and credit lines go in body[] in plan order; each plan has one ctas[] entry.

content.blog-content.description: Blog index body: the headline 'A little more to think about.', a featured post, and the list of all twenty posts as linked cards.

content.blog-content-article.description: A single blog post: title, long-form body in headed sections, and an author byline. All twenty posts share this structure.

content.legal-content.description: Body of the Privacy and Terms pages: a dated legal document ('Last updated') with a page title, an intro, a contents index and plain-language policy sections.

content.manifesto.description: The manifesto page body: a long-form, first-person story ('Less managing. More living.') in three movements (the day we know, the room Merlin makes, your time yours to spend), illustrated with four images.

features.browser.description: Home-page demonstration that Merlin can act inside a web browser: a simulated session comparing flights, ordering food and browsing a job listing, headed 'If it happens in a browser, Merlin can help.'

features.companion.description: Home-page chapter on Companion, the in-place helper: highlight text or ask about what is on screen (Option + Space) in any app, with demos in Photoshop and Finder and a rephrase-a-sentence example.

features.install-merlin-in-three-steps.description: Three illustrated install steps (open your download, move Merlin to Applications, open Merlin) that carry a new user from downloaded file to a running app.

features.meetings.description: Home-page chapter on meetings: Merlin records the call, produces a transcript, summary, key decisions and action items, then turns the outcome into PDFs, decks, spreadsheets and websites.

features.merlin-in-your-everyday.description: Shows Merlin working quietly in everyday notifications: an animated notification card with a sound toggle and a replay control, introducing the home story before the product claims begin.

features.pricing-included.description: States that every plan includes the same capabilities, as six short feature cards (context, browser, in-place help, meetings, creation, routines), so price is not read as a feature gate.

features.privacy.description: Home-page trust section 'Personal work. Private by design.': four short claims (independent audit, approval first, no model training, protection in storage and transit) that remove the privacy objection before the final call to action.

features.routines.description: Home-page story chapter 'First, a little context.': shows Merlin pulling context from connected apps (Gmail, Slack, Calendar, Linear, Notion, Granola) into a catch-up and a recurring routine, with a pause-routine control.

hero.install-intro.description: Download page opening: thanks the visitor, states that the download starts automatically, and offers fallbacks (download again, Intel Mac build) so a blocked download does not end the journey.

hero.story-hero.description: Opens the home and pricing pages with the page's promise as an h1 (home: 'Your time. Yours again.'; pricing: 'Make room for the rest of your day.'), one supporting sentence, the primary 'GET MERLIN FOR MAC' call to action on home, and the embedded hero-corner-nav (brand mark plus Pricing/Manifesto links).

proof.used-by-professionals-at.description: Social proof strip on the home page: the line 'Used by professionals at' followed by five third-party company logos (Notion, Salesforce, Harvard, HubSpot, McKinsey). Logos are real trademarks (customer-logo role, never fabricated).

shell.closing-footer.description: Closes every page except the download page: on the home page a final conversion block ('Your next free moment starts at 16:42', 'GET MERLIN FOR MAC') with an animated sky/beach scene, followed by the site-wide footer links, copyright and wordmark.

shell.install-header.description: Slim header of the download/thank-you page: the Merlin app icon only, with no navigation, so the visitor stays focused on installing.

shell.page-nav.description: Page-top container holding the main navigation (Merlin brand mark with the Pricing and Manifesto links) on every inner page. On the home and pricing pages the same hero-corner-nav is instead embedded inside hero.story-hero, so those pages have no separate page-nav node.

shell.skip-link.description: Keyboard-accessibility affordance: an off-screen link ('Skip to plans', 'Read the blog'...) that is the first focusable element and jumps past the page chrome to the page's main content anchor. One ctas[] entry: label plus #anchor href.

support.faq.description: Home-page FAQ 'Good questions. Clear answers.': a short list of getting-started and capability questions (what Merlin helps with, what is needed, own browser, how Companion works) plus an 'ask Merlin' prompt for anything else.

support.pricing-faq.description: Answers the plan and billing questions that block a purchase (which plan, what credits are, rollover, running out, annual option, how to get started) as six expandable question/answer pairs.
